intro: The Alvarado Score (MANTRELS) is a GI & Liver scoring tool used in paediatric practice. Classic clinical score for the likelihood of acute appendicitis. It scores 8 criteria and interprets the total across 4 bands, so the number always arrives with the severity it implies rather than on its own. In PediAid each criterion is shown as a labelled option with the weight it carries, so the total can be checked rather than taken on trust.
indications: Grading severity at the bedside in GI & Liver
Recording an objective severity band in the case notes
Deciding when a total crosses the threshold for escalation
Re-scoring to track whether a child is improving or deteriorating
Checking the exact criteria of a score used infrequently
method: The score sums 8 criteria: Migration of pain to RLQ; Anorexia; Nausea or vomiting; Tenderness in RLQ; Rebound pain; Elevated temperature ≥ 37.3 °C; Leucocytosis > 10 000 /µL; Shift to the left (neutrophils > 75 %). Totals are then banded: any score - Unlikely: score 0-4 - appendicitis unlikely. Consider discharge with safety-netting or an alternative diagnosis; 5 points or more - Possible: score 5-6 - compatible with appendicitis. Observation and/or imaging recommended; 7 points or more - Probable: score 7-8 - probable appendicitis. Surgical referral; 9 points or more - Very probable: score 9-10 - very probable appendicitis. Urgent surgical referral.
guidelineRefs: Total range 0-10. Less well validated in young children than the Paediatric Appendicitis Score.
Source: Alvarado A. A practical score for the early diagnosis of acute appendicitis. Ann Emerg Med 1986;15:557-64.

faqs.q: How many criteria does the Alvarado Score (MANTRELS) use?
faqs.a: 8. They are Migration of pain to RLQ; Anorexia; Nausea or vomiting; Tenderness in RLQ; Rebound pain; Elevated temperature ≥ 37.3 °C; and others.

faqs.q: What do the bands of the Alvarado Score (MANTRELS) mean?
faqs.a: The total is interpreted as: any score - Unlikely: score 0-4 - appendicitis unlikely. Consider discharge with safety-netting or an alternative diagnosis; 5 points or more - Possible: score 5-6 - compatible with appendicitis. Observation and/or imaging recommended; 7 points or more - Probable: score 7-8 - probable appendicitis. Surgical referral; 9 points or more - Very probable: score 9-10 - very probable appendicitis. Urgent surgical referral.

faqs.q: Does the score replace clinical judgement?
faqs.a: No. It is a structured way to record and communicate severity. A clinician concerned about a child should act on that concern regardless of the total.
